terra.problem: Sinning unintentionally does not necessarily mean the person did not know what they were doing.
It gives the priest's position between the people and the LORD as the reason his sin brings guilt on the people. The verse does not give that reason.
It adds that the offering must come the moment they know, with no waiting. The text does not specify that timing.
Saying the clock starts the moment they know adds a precise deadline the text does not give.
It invents a reason the elders lay hands on the bull: that the crowd cannot all lean on it at once.
The claim that the whole system points to forgiveness goes beyond what this passage says about the assembly's offering.
The pop quiz joke invokes a school scenario, which is outside the intended adult audience.
Meaning well is not stated as the leader's motive, and the claim that the way to forgiveness covers everybody goes beyond these instructions.
Saying the offering points to the LORD and not to the person bringing it overlooks the stated atonement and forgiveness for that person.
The verse says the person is unaware of the uncleanness; it does not say he did not mean to touch the object.
The instruction to say the confession out loud adds a requirement the text does not specify.
It says confession must be out loud rather than written down. The text does not specify the form of the confession.
The verse permits the bird offering but does not say the person can bring it right now or already has access to it.
The text does not say the person already has the specified offering or can bring it immediately.
Telling the baker not to add anything sounds corrective and preachy rather than warm.
